Project: Kubernetes. Upgrade being assessed: 1.23 -> 1.29.
This change was introduced in release 1.28. Source: Kubernetes v1.28.0 CHANGELOG (official_changelog). Section: v1.28.0 / Urgent Upgrade Notes / (No, really, you MUST read this before you upgrade).
Version facts from package metadata for this release (authoritative for version numbers): none

ITEM:
<<<
Action required for the custom scheduler plugin developers. Here's the breaking change in EnqueueExtension in the scheduling framework. The EventsToRegister in EnqueueExtension changed the return value from ClusterEvent to ClusterEventWithHint. ClusterEventWithHint allows each plugin to filter out more useless events via the callback function named QueueingHintFn. When the scheduling queue receives a cluster event, before moving each Pod from unschedulable pod pool to activeQ/backoffQ, it will call QueueingHintFn of plugins that rejected each Pod in the previous scheduling cycle. Depending on the value returned from QueueingHintFn, the scheduling queue changes how it queues each Pod: - if more than one QueueingHintFn returns QueueImmediately, it queues Pod to activeQ. - If no QueueingHintFn returns QueueImmediately and more than one plugin returns QueueAfterBackoff, it queues Pod to backoffQ if Pod is backing off, or to activeQ if Pod's backoff has already finished. - If all QueueingHintFn return QueueSkip, it puts this pod back to the unschedulable pod pool Having appropriate QueueingHintFn contributes to reducing useless retries and thus improves the overall scheduler's performance. How can I migrate? For backward compatibility, nil QueueingHintFn is treated as always returning QueueAfterBackoff. So, if you want to just keep the existing behavior, you can register ClusterEventWithHint with no QueueingHintFn in it. But, registering appropriate QueueingHintFn is, of course, better from a scheduling performance perspective. - CephFS volume plugin (kubernetes.io/cephfs) has been deprecated in this release and will be removed in a subsequent release. The alternative is to use the CephFS CSI driver (https://github.com/ceph/ceph-csi/) in your Kubernetes cluster. - Deprecated support for CSI migration of Ceph RBD volumes. Users who were relying on Kubernetes' ability to migrate to an out-of-tree storage driver should complete that migration before the support for it is removed. - RBD volume plugin (kubernetes.io/rbd) has been deprecated in this release and will be removed in a subsequent release. Alternative is to use RBD CSI driver (https://github.com/ceph/ceph-csi/) in your Kubernetes Cluster.
>>>

PARENT CONTEXT (same section, for disambiguation only):
<<<
(none)
>>>

Decide the disposition:
- "risk": the item describes something that can break an app/deployment, require migration work, or create operational risk.
- "context": it is accurate but needs no action at 1.29 (no user action required, deprecated-but-working, additive feature). Give the reason.

For "risk", produce one or more risk paths. Use separate paths for separate symbols/APIs when they can be checked independently. Hard rules:
1. Every condition has at least one quote copied EXACTLY, character for character, from ITEM or PARENT CONTEXT (contiguous span, 3-40 words, no ellipses, no added words). Do not fix typos or formatting.
2. Each path has exactly one condition with category "version" stating that the upgrade crosses release 1.28 (quote the text that ties the change to this release, or the change statement itself), and at least one application/deployment condition (category api_usage, configuration, dependency, runtime, deployment, database, behavior or test_coverage) describing what the app or deployment must use/have for the risk to apply.
3. If the text does not state something you need, do not assert it: use role "uncertain" and explain in ambiguities. derived_by: "extraction" when the text states the fact; for an application/deployment condition ("the application uses X"), use "extraction" when the text names X as the thing affected by the change. Use "inference" only when you infer an affected symbol, scope or impact that the text does not name. Only add ambiguities for real gaps or conflicts in the text, not for the general fact that a specific application has not been inspected.
4. role: "required" (must hold), "alternative" (any one of the alternatives suffices), "optional" (raises impact), "disqualifying" (if it holds, the risk does NOT apply, e.g. not using the new opt-in API), "uncertain".
5. operator/expected_value must be checkable: e.g. operator "present" with expected_value the literal symbol; "less_than" with a version; "equals" with a setting value. expected_value is a string.
6. If a replacement API/setting/version is named, put the migration step in suggested_actions and add a condition for any behavior that differs in the replacement when the text states one.
7. search_queries: for app-side conditions with a literal symbol, give ripgrep regexes (tool "ripgrep"), kubectl commands (tool "kubectl") or SQL (tool "sql") that would find usage. Empty list if no literal symbol.
8. primary_symbol: the most specific identifier of the change (full apiVersion string like "policy/v1beta1", setting name, function, flag, or runtime name like "Python"/"Node.js"). symbols: all identifiers involved.
9. risk_level rubric: critical = upgrade fails or data is at risk for most users meeting the conditions (e.g. unsupported runtime/database version, removed API version that stops serving); high = code or config meeting the conditions breaks at upgrade; medium = behavior change or migration with a clear workaround; low = edge case, cosmetic, or warning-only.
10. fires_at: "upgrade" (at upgrade time), "first_use" (when a feature is first exercised), "rotation" (on credential/password rotation), "rollout" (on deployment rollout), "future_removal" (deprecated now, removed later).
11. applies_to: fill upgrade_method (e.g. "pg_upgrade", "dump/restore"), cluster_type, or from_versions (a version specifier like "<3.1") ONLY if the text restricts applicability; otherwise null.
Do not output confidence.

paths.path_name: Scheduler EnqueueExtension EventsToRegister return type change
paths.description: Custom scheduler plugins whose EventsToRegister in EnqueueExtension returns ClusterEvent must change to ClusterEventWithHint, a breaking change in the scheduling framework.

conditions.statement: Upgrade crosses release 1.28, the release in which the EventsToRegister return type change was introduced
quotes: The EventsToRegister in EnqueueExtension changed the return value from ClusterEvent to ClusterEventWithHint.
conditions.relevance: Release 1.28 is stated by the source metadata for this change, and the upgrade 1.23 to 1.29 crosses it.

conditions.statement: Custom scheduler plugin implements EnqueueExtension EventsToRegister returning ClusterEvent
quotes: Action required for the custom scheduler plugin developers.
conditions.relevance: Only plugins that implement EnqueueExtension are affected by the return type change.
ambiguities: The text does not state which return type existing plugins use in 1.23; check plugin source.

conditions.statement: Plugin registers ClusterEventWithHint with a nil QueueingHintFn
quotes: For backward compatibility, nil QueueingHintFn is treated as always returning QueueAfterBackoff.
conditions.relevance: With a nil QueueingHintFn the existing requeue behavior is preserved, so the queueing behavior change does not apply.

suggested_actions: Change EventsToRegister to return ClusterEventWithHint instead of ClusterEvent.
Register an appropriate QueueingHintFn for each ClusterEventWithHint to reduce useless retries.
To keep existing behavior, register ClusterEventWithHint with no QueueingHintFn.
